assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ionising radiation
items.clue: Has enough energy to knock electrons out of atoms.

items.label: Infrared radiation
items.clue: Emitted by all objects because of their temperature.

items.label: Radiation dose
items.clue: A measure of the risk of harm from exposure, in sieverts.

items.label: Normal
items.clue: A construction line at right angles to the boundary where the ray meets it.

questions.stem: The electromagnetic spectrum is described as continuous. What does this mean?

options.text: It is made of seven separate waves with gaps between them
It jumps in seven fixed steps like rungs on a ladder
Every group in it can be detected by the human eye
There are no gaps between one group and the next

questions.explanation: Wavelength changes smoothly across the spectrum, so the groups merge into one another with no gaps.

questions.stem: A student compares the infrared radiation emitted by the four faces of a Leslie cube. Which change would most improve the investigation?

options.text: Keep the detector the same distance from every face when reading it.
Move the detector closer to the darker faces so their readings are clearer.
Take the reading from each of the faces at a different water temperature.
Use a separate metal cube for each of the four surfaces tested.

questions.explanation: Distance is a control variable: the reading falls as the detector is moved away, so it must be fixed if only the surface is to change.

questions.stem: Ultraviolet waves, X-rays and gamma rays can have hazardous effects on human body tissue. What do those effects depend on?

options.text: The size of the dose received, whatever type it is
Only the total size of the dose, not its type
The distance the radiation travelled to the body
The type of radiation and the size of the dose

questions.explanation: The specification states that the effects depend on the type of radiation and the size of the dose.

questions.stem: How does a microwave oven cook food?

options.text: Microwaves heat the middle of the food first
Microwaves make the food slightly radioactive
An element's red glow is the infrared that cooks it
The food absorbs microwaves and heats up

questions.explanation: Microwaves are absorbed by the food, and the energy transferred raises its temperature.

questions.stem: Which list gives the electromagnetic groups in order from longest wavelength to shortest?

options.text: Radio, microwave, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, X-rays, gamma
Radio, microwave, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays
Gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwave, radio
Radio, microwave, infrared, violet, red, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma

questions.explanation: This is the order given in the specification, going from long to short wavelength.

questions.stem: Four identical cans are painted matt black, matt white, shiny silver and dull grey. Each is filled with cold water and placed the same distance from a radiant heater. Which can's water warms fastest?

options.text: The shiny silver can, because a polished metal surface takes radiation in best.
The matt black can, because it is the best absorber of infrared.
All four cans equally, because the heater is the same distance away.
The dull grey can, because a metal surface draws radiation in fastest.

questions.explanation: Matt black is the best absorber, so it takes in radiation from the heater at the greatest rate and warms fastest.

questions.stem: A patient receives a radiation dose of 75 mSv from a scan. Use 1000 millisieverts (mSv) = 1 sievert (Sv). What is this dose in sieverts?

options.text: 7.5 Sv
75 Sv

questions.explanation: 75 divided by 1000 gives 0.075 Sv, using the relationship 1000 mSv = 1 Sv as given in the stem.

questions.stem: An electric grill glows red and cooks the food placed underneath it. Which radiation transfers energy to the food?

options.text: Microwaves, because all cookers use microwaves
Infrared, which is absorbed by the food surface
Ultraviolet, because the element glows white
Radio waves, because they carry heat energy

questions.explanation: The specification pairs infrared with electrical heaters and cooking food; the hot element emits infrared, which the surface of the food absorbs.

questions.stem: Moving across the spectrum from radio waves towards gamma rays, what happens to wavelength and frequency?

options.text: Wavelength decreases and frequency increases
Wavelength and frequency both increase together
Wavelength rises while the frequency falls
Both wavelength and frequency decrease

questions.explanation: Going from long to short wavelength is the same as going from low to high frequency.

questions.stem: A ray of light travels through air and strikes the flat surface of a glass block at an angle to the normal. Light travels more slowly in glass than in air. Which statement correctly describes the refracted ray inside the glass?

options.text: It bends towards the normal, because it slows down in the glass.
It bends away from the normal as it enters the glass.
It carries straight on undeviated, changing only its speed.
It reflects off the surface without entering the glass at all.

questions.stem: The table shows the average dose a person in the UK receives each year: radon gas 1.3 mSv, medical X-rays 0.4 mSv, cosmic rays 0.3 mSv. Which conclusion is supported by these data?

options.text: Medical X-rays give the largest yearly dose of the three
The three sources together give a dose of over one sievert
Radon gives a larger yearly dose than the other two added
Cosmic rays carry the greatest risk as they come from space

questions.explanation: 1.3 mSv is greater than 0.4 mSv + 0.3 mSv = 0.7 mSv, so this conclusion does follow from the data given.

questions.stem: An infrared camera is used to find a person standing in a dark field at night. Why does the person show up on the image?

options.text: The camera shines visible light on the person
Infrared from the body can be seen by the eye too
The person reflects ultraviolet from the night sky above
Their body gives out infrared that the camera detects

questions.explanation: The specification pairs infrared with infrared cameras; a warm body emits infrared, which the camera detects even in total darkness.

questions.stem: A sound wave travelling through the air arrives at a person's ear. Which statement describes how this leads to the sensation of sound?

options.text: The ear drum turns the wave straight into electricity and never moves
The wave passes on unchanged along the ear canal and into the brain
The wave makes the ear drum and other parts of the ear vibrate
The ear amplifies the wave until it is loud enough to hear

questions.explanation: Within the ear, sound waves cause the ear drum and other parts to vibrate, which causes the sensation of sound.

questions.stem: Survey waves pass easily through rock layer X but are strongly absorbed by rock layer Y. How does this difference help the team explore ground they cannot see?

options.text: A weak returning signal shows the waves went through layer Y
Strong absorption sends back a stronger reflection from layer Y
Layer Y reflects every wave, so nothing returns from below
Both layers return the same signal, so absorption is no use

questions.stem: Which statement about how substances behave towards electromagnetic waves is correct?

options.text: A substance that fails to transmit a wave must have absorbed the whole of it.
One substance can reflect one wavelength but absorb a different one.
A wave behaves in just the same way in every substance it meets.
A clear substance will transmit every wavelength reaching it.

questions.explanation: This is what the specification means by behaviour varying with wavelength: a single substance treats different wavelengths differently.

questions.stem: (HT only) A radio wave is absorbed by an aerial joined to a circuit. What may the wave create in that circuit?

options.text: A steady direct current, always one way
An alternating current in that circuit
A magnetic field but no current in it
A current whose frequency is doubled

questions.explanation: The specification states that absorbed radio waves may create an alternating current, so they induce oscillations in the circuit.

questions.stem: (HT only) An energy efficient lamp produces ultraviolet inside its tube, yet the room is lit by visible light. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: A coating absorbs ultraviolet and emits visible light
The lamp is designed to send ultraviolet into the room
The ultraviolet itself is the light you see the room by
Ultraviolet slows down in the tube, becoming visible light

questions.explanation: The fluorescent coating on the inside of the tube absorbs the ultraviolet and re-emits the energy as visible light, so the room is lit without ultraviolet leaving the lamp.

questions.stem: A bat call at 45 kHz is played to a class through an ultrasonic transducer at very high intensity. Nobody in the room hears anything. What is the best explanation?

options.text: The sound is far too quiet by the time that it has reached anybody's ear
A 45 kHz pressure wave in air is not a sound wave, so there is nothing to hear
Only very high frequencies are lost, and hearing them can be trained back
The ear cannot convert a wave of that frequency into vibrations

questions.explanation: The conversion of sound waves to vibrations of solids works over a limited frequency range, and this restricts the limits of human hearing.
